articles.summary: El chef explica cómo conseguir una tortilla de patata más jugosa con mantequilla
articles.body: La tortilla de patata es uno de los platos más representativos de la gastronomía española y también uno de los que más debates genera entre quienes disfrutan cocinando. La elección de los ingredientes, el grosor de las patatas, el uso de cebolla y, sobre todo, el punto de cuajado son algunos de los aspectos que dividen a los aficionados a esta receta. Conseguir una tortilla jugosa por dentro sin que quede demasiado hecha es uno de los objetivos más habituales. Para lograrlo, el chef Dani García ha compartido varios trucos a través de su sección 'Cocinando con haters', en la que prepara recetas mientras responde a las críticas que recibe en redes sociales. Entre sus recomendaciones destaca un cambio en la forma de cuajar la tortilla: utilizar mantequilla en lugar de aceite de oliva. Según explica el cocinero, la elección de la grasa influye en el resultado final y permite adaptar la textura de la tortilla a los gustos de cada persona. El chef malagueño defiende que la mantequilla es una buena opción para quienes prefieren una tortilla más blanda y cremosa. "La mantequilla transmite menos calor que el aceite porque a mí me gusta blandita. Si os gusta tostada, pues echadle aceite", explica en el vídeo. De esta manera, García plantea una alternativa para quienes buscan una textura menos cuajada, frente a quienes prefieren una tortilla más hecha y con una superficie tostada. La clave está en adaptar la técnica al resultado que se quiera conseguir, sin dar por hecho que existe un único punto perfecto para todos los paladares. Sin embargo, la mantequilla no es el único elemento que el cocinero incorpora a su receta. También propone prestar atención a la preparación de las patatas y a su integración con el huevo, dos pasos que considera importantes para conseguir un buen resultado. Para empezar, Dani García recomienda cortar las patatas en rodajas finas. Una vez fritas, deben incorporarse directamente al huevo batido. Después, hay que remover la mezcla y dejarla reposar durante aproximadamente 25 minutos. Este tiempo permite que las patatas se integren con el huevo antes de pasar a la sartén. El chef también introduce otro ingrediente en su preparación: una mayonesa elaborada con huevo, aceite de oliva, vinagre de Jerez y sal, que añade a la mezcla reservada de patata y huevo. Otro de los consejos que comparte Dani García está relacionado con uno de los momentos que más dificultades pueden generar al cocinar este plato: darle la vuelta a la tortilla. Para facilitar el proceso, recomienda poner un poco de agua y aceite de oliva en el plato que se vaya a utilizar. Es un gesto sencillo que forma parte de su método para manipular la tortilla durante la cocción.

articles.title: After years of backlash, Apu returns to 'The Simpsons' with a South Asian voice
articles.summary: Across 38 seasons of “The Simpsons,” the Halloween-themed “Treehouse of Horror” episodes have always been a treat of spooky stand-alone storylines.
articles.body: Across 38 seasons of “The Simpsons,” the Halloween-themed “Treehouse of Horror” episodes have always been a treat of spooky stand-alone storylines. On Sunday, the show surprised viewers with a major resurrection: Apu, the beloved Kwik-E-Mart operator who had not been heard for the better part of a decade, spoke once again in Springfield. He and his wife, Manjula, were back with a meaty plotline — and the voices of actual Indian American actors: Sunil Malhotra, a veteran voice-over artist, and Janina Gavankar (“The Morning Show”). “Bringing Apu back feels like a reclamation. It truly IS his homecoming,” Malhotra and Gavankar said Sunday in a joint Instagram post. Apu's unheralded return is a remarkable twist to a yearslong discourse about how the character has represented a painful stereotype for some South Asian Americans. After a 2017 documentary by comedian Hari Kondabolu, “The Problem With Apu,” the character was largely exiled from the screen. How a documentary on Apu became a turning point In “The Problem With Apu,” Kondabolu, a self-described fan of the Fox show, tried to process his misgivings. He interviewed a slew of celebrities of South Asian origin, including Kal Penn, Utkarsh Ambudkar and Hasan Minhaj, about growing up with the character. They shared memories of being bullied and called “Apu” as an insult. Adding to their view of Apu as just a caricature was that Hank Azaria, a white actor, voiced him. With the full name of Apu Nahasapeemapetilon Jr., he felt like the “forever foreigner, someone who represents Indians in the United States through this sole typology of being a convenience store owner, being a recent immigrant, having this heavy accent, being really limited in this sort of like American identity,” says Bhoomi Thakore, an assistant professor of sociology at the University of Connecticut. Thakore notes that Kondabolu's film raised the notion that Apu was the only portrayal of an Indian character most people knew when he debuted in 1990. Azaria stepped away from the role after the documentary, continuing to voice other “Simpsons” characters, as Apu fell silent, seen only in the background. Kondabolu, however, had never called for Apu to be canceled. On Monday, he praised “The Simpsons” for devising “a clever solution to all this” and hiring Malhotra and Gavankar. “I’m also still proud of the public conversation about race and representation my documentary started,” he told The Associated Press in an emailed statement. “Finally, I’m hoping this stops all the hatemail in many languages that has been sent my way over the past decade.” After years in the background, Apu appears here to stay In a 2018 episode, “The Simpsons” responded to Kondabolu's documentary by having Lisa Simpson bemoan how “something that started decades ago and was applauded and inoffensive is now politically incorrect. ... What can you do?” The camera then panned to a framed photo of Apu. The gag was branded by some as weak for not directly addressing the controversy. In a 2020 New York Times interview, Azaria, who by then hadn't voiced Apu in a few years, announced he would bow out because “it just didn't feel right.” Later that year, in response to racial reckoning demonstrations, “The Simpsons” announced it would no longer cast white voice actors as characters of color. The show then recast two Black characters, Carl Carlson and Dr. Julius Hibbert, with Black actors. Kondabolu had not spoken with “The Simpsons” producers about Apu’s comeback, he confirmed to the AP, “but they didn’t owe me that.” And it does sound like Apu is here to stay. “We love this character and wanted to bring him back in a smart, Simpsons-y way that allowed him to evolve,” executive producer Matt Selman said in a statement. “We’re excited by what Sunil has already brought to the role and look forward to seeing more of Apu in the future.” Apu was also embraced by South Asians, despite the controversy A few weeks after “The Simpsons” responded to the documentary, author and producer Amar Shah wrote a series of social media posts and then a Washington Post op-ed on why he felt mostly sentimental toward Apu. When he watched Apu, he thought of his own Indian father hard at work as a convenience store owner and how that shaped his Florida childhood. “Apu even now is a character that I wouldn't mind my kids seeing represented because they'll see aspects of themselves and of their own grandparents,” says Shah, reflecting on his 2018 piece. “I can totally empathize with someone of South Asian origin having a different POV [point of view] than me but this is my childhood. This is my story.” After watching this latest episode, Shah didn't sense any significant difference with Malhotra's performance. “Obviously, there's a different voice, tenor, texture and all that. But, the character is always going to be there, his genuine humanity,” Shah says. “I think if they had incorporated this change earlier, it would have been a lot better.” At a time of anti-South Asian hate, Apu's return is welcomed Apu is being revived amid a climate of rising anti-South Asian and Indian hate. Stop AAPI Hate and other research groups have found online use of racist slurs and threats against South Asians and Indians have jumped in the past few years. Texas Railroad Commission candidate Bo French, a Republican, recently posted a photo of South Asian University of Texas students cheering at a football game and called them “a problem.” Just last week, a man was charged with planning a mass shooting at a Hindu temple outside Chicago. Against that backdrop, Shah welcomes the show's careful approach reincarnating the character. “It's great to see that the show has evolved in time and now, especially with the discrimination and, really, the targeting of South Asians and Indian Americans as of late — questioning our patriotism, our American identity and even whether we're college football fans,” he says. The return also coincides with much more representation of prominent South Asian Americans, such as actor and showrunner Mindy Kaling, and people who have broken barriers in office, like New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and former Vice President Kamala Harris. When Apu first appeared, says University of Virginia associate professor of media studies Shilpa Davé, he was one of the only consistent representations of South Asians on TV. Now, she says, “South Asians have become a part of the landscape from ‘Bridgerton’ to … ‘Never Have I Ever’ and there’s a plethora of different kinds of representation.”

articles.title: Disney+ Rivals producer wants 'bonkbuster' shows to 'keep going forever'
articles.summary: Production bosses say the popular author's works could help make shows forever.
articles.body:
More of Dame Jilly Cooper's "bonkbusters" are set to be adapted for television.

The production company behind Rivals has secured the rights to the late author's entire Rutshire Chronicles series.

Rivals has been a huge success for Disney+, with huge stars including David Tennant, Emily Atack, Aidan Turner, Katherine Parkinson and Danny Dyer appearing in the show.

Dominic Treadwell-Collins, executive producer, said "We have got all these books to plunder" and "we can make it go forever".

The writer – known for what her fans call "bonkbusters" including Riders and Polo – died after sustaining a fatal head injury during a fall at her Gloucestershire home in October last year aged 88.

Dame Jilly was known for her steamy fiction focusing on scandal and adultery in upper-class society.

Who is in charge at Gloucester City Council?

Gloucester Assize of Ale looking for 'conner'

Dozens of homes approved despite dust worries

Treadwell-Collins was speaking at an event at Cheltenham Literature Festival to celebrate the literary work of Dame Jilly.

"We have got the rights to all four of the Rutshire Chronicles and it's interesting that if you look on the poster Disney have changed it to 'based upon Jilly Cooper's Rutshire Chronicles' and not upon the Rivals," Treadwell-Collins said.

"We have her blessing, we have got the family who we keep talking to, and what we are doing is taking bits of the books and repurposing them, playing around with them, but she's there as this Jilly treasure trove.

"So, we would like to keep going forever."

The writer had already approved the main storylines for the third series of Rivals before her death, Treadwell-Collins said.

"We have Jilly's notes for season one and all the way through season two, we talked to her about our plans for season three and beyond," he said.

"We have her seal of approval on big story points."

Treadwell-Collins revealed the adaptation of Rivals happened after he wrote Dame Jilly a "love letter" explaining how much he had loved her novels and how he would bring Rivals to life on TV.

"I always thought they would make brilliant television as she was such a brilliant storyteller with brilliant creative characters," he said.

"All the way through my career I have been mocked for suggesting it, television producers would laugh at me.

"Thank God they did because I kept it to myself for years.

"We went to see her, she said, 'You've got to write this, you've got to adapt this Dominic because you are a writer'.

"I've written one show myself before, I wasn't confident, I was thinking lots of other writers should write it.

"Jilly's made me a writer, that's really, really special.

"To bring that joy to Jilly Cooper is the proudest thing I've ever done, ever."

Filming for series two of Rivals took place across Bristol, Corsham in Wiltshire and Berkeley Castle in Gloucestershire, with locations across the West of England standing in for the Cotswolds and London.

David Tennant and Claire Rushbrook were seen filming scenes on the high-street of Corsham, which saw the town hall transformed into a polling station for the show.

articles.title: Who was Karthik Sabesh? Inside the life and film career of the late Tamil actor, son of composer Sabesh and nephew of late composer Deva
articles.summary: Tamil cinema has lost actor Karthik Sabesh at the age of 37, bringing fresh grief to a family known for its contributions to the film industry.
articles.body: Tamil cinema has lost actor Karthik Sabesh at the age of 37, bringing fresh grief to a family known for its contributions to the film industry. The actor, who appeared in several Tamil films, died following health issues, according to reports. His death comes just days after the passing of veteran music composer Deva, his uncle, on October 17, 2026. The family had also lost Karthik’s father, music composer MC Sabesan, in October 2025. The back-to-back losses have left their relatives and well-wishers mourning another untimely death.Karthik Sabesh’s early life and film careerKarthik Sabesh was an Indian actor who made his film debut with 'Dreams' alongside Dhanush in 2004. Being the son of music composer M. C. Sabesan, also popular as Sabesh, he ventured into the Tamil movie industry and made appearances in supporting roles in various films. His appearances have been in movies including 'Dham,' 'Kadhal Solla Vandhen,' 'Kulir 100 Degree,' 'Vallavan,' 'Pattathu Yaanai,' 'Udhayam NH4,' and 'Burma.' He has also made appearances in the Telugu movie 'Thakita Thakita' (2010).Although he did not have a long list of lead roles, his appearances in these films made him a familiar face to some Tamil cinema audiences. Karthik largely stayed away from the spotlight outside his acting work.What happened to Karthik Sabesh? According to The Hindu, Karthik Sabesh died due to health-related complications. He was 37 at the time of his death. He is survived by his wife, Ramya Karthik, and their two daughters, Prishanithara and Hairanithara. His sisters, Geetha Sabesh and Archana Sabesh, are also among the family members grieving his loss. Reports said his last rites were scheduled to take place at the Valasaravakkam crematorium in Chennai at around 4.30 pm on October 20. His sudden demise has prompted condolences from people associated with the Tamil film industry.Karthik Sabesh’s familyKarthik Sabesh belonged to a family with strong roots in Tamil film music. His father, M. C. Sabesan, worked with his brother Murali as the music director duo Sabesh-Murali. The pair composed music for films including 'Samuthiram,' 'Naina,' 'Thavamai Thavamirundhu,' 'Imsai Arasan 23 am Pulikesi,' 'Indralogathil Na Azhagappan,' and 'Pokkisham.' Sabesh died in October 2025 after health issues.His brother, Deva, also widely recognized as Thenisai Thendral, died on October 17, 2026, when he was 75 years old, due to heart failure. He was one of the well-known composers of some famous soundtracks like 'Baashha', 'Annamalai', and 'Aasai'.The death of Karthik Sabesh means another sad story to the family, with the loss of members of both generations in the family.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Pedro Torrijos, escritor, no confía en 'La bola negra' y pronostica la sorpresa de los Oscar: "Va a ganar hasta el de Mejor Actriz de Reparto"
articles.standfirst: Pronostica el éxito de 'You Can See Everything', el documental sobre Elizabeth Holmes
articles.summary: Pronostica el éxito de 'You Can See Everything', el documental sobre Elizabeth Holmes
articles.body: Pedro Torrijos ha compartido en X un pronóstico inesperado sobre la próxima edición de los Oscar. El escritor y divulgador ha reaccionado a la campaña de 'You Can See Everything', una producción documental que aspira a competir en numerosas categorías de los premios de Hollywood, y ha apuntado a que podría convertirse en una de las grandes sorpresas de la temporada. El comentario de Torrijos llega después de que la cuenta especializada en cine Film Updates publicara una lista con las categorías en las que la película será presentada para optar a los galardones. Entre ellas figuran Mejor Película, Mejor Dirección, Mejor Actriz de Reparto y Mejor Documental, además de otras categorías técnicas. "Que si La Odisea, que si La Bola Negra, y al final va a ganar los Óscar un documental sobre un caso semiolvidado hecho por un tipo rarísimo...", ha escrito Torrijos. A continuación, ha insistido en su predicción: "Va a ganar hasta el de Mejor Actriz de Reparto, un documental... y sí, esto es un (casi)spoiler". Con estas palabras, el divulgador contrapone dos de los títulos que concentran parte de la conversación cinematográfica con una producción documental que, a su juicio, podría terminar imponiéndose en la carrera por los premios. La campaña de 'You Can See Everything' contempla su presentación en 11 categorías: Mejor Película, Mejor Dirección, Mejor Actriz de Reparto, Mejor Documental, Mejor Diseño de Producción, Mejor Fotografía, Mejor Diseño de Vestuario, Mejor Montaje, Mejor Maquillaje y Peluquería, Mejor Sonido y Mejor Banda Sonora Original. La amplitud de la campaña resulta llamativa, especialmente por la inclusión de Mejor Película y Mejor Actriz de Reparto junto a Mejor Documental. La posibilidad de competir en varias categorías no implica, sin embargo, que la producción vaya a conseguir nominaciones. Las candidaturas oficiales se conocerán cuando la Academia de Hollywood publique la lista definitiva. 'You Can See Everything' se centra en Elizabeth Holmes, la fundadora de Theranos condenada por fraude a inversores, y en las semanas previas a su entrada en prisión en 2023. Holmes invita a los cineastas Nathan Fielder y Lance Oppenheim a documentar su vida privada junto a su pareja, Billy Evans, en un periodo marcado por su condena y las consecuencias del escándalo empresarial. Theranos llegó a alcanzar una valoración multimillonaria gracias a la promesa de desarrollar una tecnología capaz de realizar numerosos análisis médicos con unas pocas gotas de sangre. Sin embargo, las investigaciones revelaron que la empresa había exagerado las capacidades de sus dispositivos y Holmes acabó siendo condenada por fraude. La película va más allá del relato sobre la caída de la empresaria y explora la forma en que Holmes presenta su propia historia, así como la relación entre la imagen pública, la percepción de la verdad y la manipulación. Dirigido por Fielder y Oppenheim, el documental combina el acceso a la intimidad de sus protagonistas con un planteamiento que cuestiona los límites entre realidad y representación.

articles.title: Princess Diana feared Prince Harry would ‘wither’ in Prince William’s shadow: expert
articles.summary: Princess Diana worried Prince Harry would "wither" in Prince William's shadow, says royal expert, as secret 1991 recordings surface in new documentary.
articles.body: Princess Diana feared Prince Harry would struggle to find his place in the royal family while growing up in the shadow of his older brother and future king Prince William, according to a royal expert. The late Princess of Wales’ concerns about her sons are back in the spotlight amid news of the upcoming three-part documentary "Diana Unheard," which will feature never-before-heard audio from roughly five hours of secret recordings that Diana made with her friend Dr. James Colthurst in 1991. The documentary's producers told Deadline that the recordings, which were used in Andrew Morton’s explosive 1992 biography, "Diana: Her True Story," include the princess speaking candidly about her sons, William and the line of succession, as well as her troubled marriage to then-Prince Charles and other aspects of royal life. PRINCE HARRY'S RUMORED DIANA FILM 'MIGHT FEEL LIKE ANOTHER BETRAYAL' TO PRINCE WILLIAM AS RIFT GROWS: EXPERT While speaking with Fox News Digital, British royals expert Christopher Andersen shared his view that the recordings could reveal Diana's long-held concerns about the vastly different paths awaiting her sons. "Diana worried from the beginning that Harry might wither in the shadow of his brother the future king," the "Kate!" author said. PRINCE WILLIAM'S ABSENCE SPEAKS VOLUMES AS KING CHARLES REUNITES WITH PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE: EXPERTS "Even at a young age, William shared his mother's concerns and for the most part took great pains to spare his brother's feelings," Andersen continued. "It's very telling that, in his last conversation with Diana just hours before her death, William expressed his fear that a photo opportunity at Eton might leave Harry feeling ignored." Diana died at age 36 in August 1997 after suffering injuries sustained in a car accident in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris, France. Her partner, Dodi Fayed, and the driver, Henri Paul, also died in the crash. KING CHARLES, PRINCE WILLIAM 'FURIOUS' AS PRINCESS DIANA'S BROTHER UNLEASHES EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS: EXPERTS Hours before her death, Diana called William, then 15, from her hotel in Paris, according to Morton's biography. During what would become their final conversation, William reportedly told his mother that he had been asked to participate in a solo photocall to mark the beginning of his third year at Eton College and shared that he was deeply concerned the high-profile solo moment would make Harry, then 12, feel overshadowed and excluded. According to Andersen, Diana had confidence that William, now 44, would succeed in his role as future king, but she was apprehensive over how the monarchy's heir-and-spare dynamic would affect Harry, now 42. PRINCE GEORGE FOLLOWS PRINCE WILLIAM'S FOOTSTEPS AT ETON IN A CHANGING ROYAL WORLD: EXPERTS "Wise, sensitive, an old soul — these were some of the words that Diana used to describe William," Andersen said. "She saw him as being mature far beyond his years. While Diana knew much would be demanded of William in the future, she never doubted that he would be up to the task." "Harry was another matter entirely," Andersen said. "The world saw Harry as a charming scamp, and there definitely was that side to him, but Diana knew better than anyone that always being in his brother's formidable shadow could leave the Spare with deep-seated feelings of insecurity and gnawing self-doubt." PRINCE WILLIAM'S DOOR IS 'BOLTED SHUT' AS PRINCE HARRY PLANS UK RETURN WITH MEGHAN MARKLE, CHILDREN: EXPERT However, Andersen expressed his opinion that Diana had faith in the strength of the bond between William and Harry and would not have foreseen their future estrangement. "Looking back, it's so odd to remember how close the brothers truly were," he said. "They had their moments, as all siblings do, but the boys were always so emotionally dependent on each other." PRINCE WILLIAM AND KATE MIDDLETON 'PLAYING IT COOL' AS PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE RETURN TO THE UK: EXPERT "Diana always felt that, whatever challenges they faced, William and Harry would weather the storm together," Andersen continued. "She viewed the brothers as a unit. As far as Diana was concerned, theirs was an unbreakable bond." Royal expert Kinsey Schofield agreed that Diana did not fear that there would be a rift between the brothers but argued that the late princess worried more over William's burden as the future king than Harry's supporting role. PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON FACE 'SUSSEX CIRCUS' AS PRINCE GEORGE PREPARES FOR ETON: EXPERT "Based on my research, Diana was more concerned about the pressures of royal life affecting her sons individually than the possibility of them becoming estranged," the host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered" told Fox News Digital. "Diana understood that William and Harry were destined for very different lives," Schofield continued. "William was born to be king. Harry was born to support him. She wanted them to remain close because she understood the importance of William having someone he could trust." PRINCE HARRY’S PUSH TO GIVE ARCHIE, LILIBET ROYAL UPBRINGING EXPOSES ‘CONTRADICTION’ AFTER PALACE EXIT: EXPERT "Prince William’s future weighed heavily on Diana because she understood the responsibility he would inherit," she added. "She knew that William would never have the freedom to simply walk away from his destiny. She spoke to him about the importance of finding a suitable and supportive partner. She believed in his leadership but worried about his reluctance as a child." "Harry, on the other hand, had opportunities William would never enjoy. He could pursue his own interests, build a career around charitable causes, and enjoy a degree of independence that his brother couldn’t." Schofield pointed out that Harry was once a favorite of the British public and celebrated for his achievements. "He was enormously popular," Schofield said. "He had a successful military career, founded the Invictus Games, and was one of the most beloved members of the royal family." "Harry wasn’t destined for failure because he was born second," she continued. "He had every opportunity to build a meaningful life within the institution." "I think Diana would have been more concerned about William carrying the weight of the Crown than Harry having to share the spotlight," Schofield added. The royal experts agreed that Diana would have been shocked and distraught over William and Harry's current estrangement. "Diana would have been heartbroken, and it's hard for me to imagine that the split ever would have happened if she had been alive," Andersen said. "Things just wouldn't have gotten so out of hand." "I think Diana would be devastated," Schofield told Fox News Digital. "Prince William and Harry shared an experience that very few people on earth could understand. They lost their mother in front of the entire world. That shared grief should have been something that united them for life." Reports of tensions between the brothers first emerged in 2018, with Harry publicly acknowledging the strain in their relationship the following year when he said the brothers were on "different paths." The divide widened further after Harry and his wife Meghan Markle announced their decision to step down from their roles as working royals in January 2020. The two's relationship continued to deteriorate in subsequent years following Harry and Markle's bombshell 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey, the couple's 2022 Netflix series "Harry & Meghan" and Harry's explosive 2023 memoir "Spare." However, British royals expert Hilary Fordwich cautioned against viewing Diana's decades-old concerns through the lens of events that unfolded long after her death. "Hearing tapes today made back in 1991 though shouldn’t be taken as a current verdict regarding events and complicated results of events Princess Diana isn’t tragically alive to witness," Fordwich told Fox News Digital. While Diana herself was known for challenging royal conventions and became increasingly more independent following her 1992 separation from Charles, she continued carrying out public duties and remained committed to many of the causes she had championed as a working royal. Andersen and Schofield argued that Diana's rebellious streak does not necessarily mean she would have supported Harry's decision to leave royal duties and his subsequent actions. "Diana definitely knew that Harry would have to forge his own path to some extent — certainly more so than William, whose role in royal life is preordained," Andersen said. "But I don't believe Diana would have approved of Harry abruptly bailing on the monarchy the way he did." "True, Diana was a rule-breaker and a rebel, but she also had a strong sense of duty and of history," he continued. "Diana believed that Harry had an important role to play. Harry probably would never be king, but he was the son of one and, as such, had his own unique destiny to fulfill within the monarchy." "Diana might have sympathized with Harry’s frustrations, but I don’t believe that means she would have supported everything he’s done since leaving," Schofield said. articles.title: Rayna Vallandingham, campeona mundial de taekwondo y villana en 'Street Fighter': "Quiero romper estereotipos"
articles.standfirst: La californiana ha sido trece veces campeona del mundo
articles.summary: La californiana ha sido trece veces campeona del mundo
articles.body: Rayna Vallandingham es una artista marcial y una actriz muy conocida por los aficionados a las películas y series de acción. La californiana, cinturón negro de cuarto Dan, ha sido trece veces campeona del mundo de Taekwondo en torneos organizados por la Asociación Americana de Taekwondo (ATA). Ganó su primer título a la edad de ocho años, ahora tiene 23, y desde entonces su carrera deportiva y profesional ha avanzado en clara línea ascendente. Su último proyecto, interpretar a Juli, una de las villanas en la última película de 'Street Fighter', que ya está en los cines españoles. Rayna Vallandingham, además de formar parte del reparto en 'Street Fighter', ha aparecido en numeras producciones con anterioridad. La más reciente es la serie 'Cobra Kai', aunque también ha tenido papeles en 'Underdog Kids', 'Citadel', 'Clout', o 'Pawns', entre otras series, películas y vídeos musicales. Por otra parte, su presencia en redes sociales es muy notable: acumula tres millones y medio de seguidores sólo en Instagram. La actriz, de ascendencia india, se ha mostrado satisfecha de haber conseguido romper con los prejuicios que existe con artistas indias. "Siempre es la chica de instituto con padres protectores... Y este no es mi caso en absoluto. Quiero romper estos estereotipos. Si algún día tengo una hija, debe saber que puede hacer lo que ella quiera, que no hay ninguna caja en la que deba encajar. Eso lo significaría todo para mí", ha afirmado en declaraciones recogidas por The National Arts. La californiana ha confesado que el Taekwondo, deporte en el que ha sido campeona mundial en trece ocasiones, tiene una importa capital para ella. "Para mí, el taekwondo no es sólo un deporte o un arte estéticamente agradable; es un sentimiento. Es mi refugio seguro, un lugar al que puedo acudir cuando me siento perdida para poder volver a encontrarme", ha afirmado Rayna Vallandingham en una entrevista a The Pocket Magazine. El personaje de Juli, en los videojuegos en los que se basa la película 'Street Fighter', es una asesina bajo el control de M.Bison, el gran villano de la saga creada por Capcom. Forma parte de su guardia de élite. La primera aparición de Juli, interpretada por Rayna Vallandingham, llegó en el videojuego 'Street Fighter Alpha 3', lanzado en el año 1998 en las salas de arcade y en la consola PlayStation.

articles.title: ‘Kalank’, 'Nayyi Naveli' to ‘Adipurush’: Bollywood films that capture the spirit of Dussehra with grand celebrations, good vs evil and mythological drama
articles.summary: Dasara is more than just a festival on the calendar; it is a story of good triumphing over evil, and Bollywood has long drawn on that idea.
articles.body: Dasara is more than just a festival on the calendar; it is a story of good triumphing over evil, and Bollywood has long drawn on that idea. From grand Ravan Dahan scenes set to soulful music to dark tales of obsession and revenge, and from mythological retellings to supernatural comedies, several Hindi films capture the spirit of the festival in different ways. Whether you want a regal, festive backdrop or a tale of dharma versus adharma, these films offer a watchlist that brings Dasara vibes to your screen.'Kalank''Kalank' captures the beauty of Dasara through the song 'Ghar More Pardesiya,' featuring Alia Bhatt as Roop and Varun Dhawan as Zafar. The scene takes place amid traditional festivities, with a towering Ravan effigy burning in the background as the characters cross paths. The grand costumes, warm lighting, traditional music, and elaborate period setting create a regal, almost dreamlike festive atmosphere.'Ek Villain''Ek Villain' is more about darkness, obsession, loss, and revenge than about Dasara itself. Unlike films that prominently show Ravan Dahan, it does not have a similarly well-established iconic Dasara sequence. However, its intense atmosphere, morally complicated characters, and the contrast between love and violence can evoke the darker side of the festival’s symbolism: the battle between good and evil within human beings.'Nayyi Naveli''Nayyi Naveli,' starring Yami Gautam, blends supernatural comedy, family drama, and Indian mythological references. Its story follows Mohini, a newly married woman whose in-laws begin to suspect that she is a witch, while the truth behind her husband adds another layer of mystery. The film draws on the cultural atmosphere surrounding Ram, Ravan, and Dussehra, making it particularly relevant to the festival. Its appeal lies in the contrast between the image of an ideal Indian bride and the possibility of something dark hiding beneath the surface.'Adipurush''Adipurush' is rooted in the Ramayana, the epic most directly associated with the traditional meaning of Dasara. Prabhas plays Raghav, a character based on Lord Ram, while Saif Ali Khan plays Lankesh, inspired by Ravan. The conflict between Raghav and Lankesh reflects the battle between dharma and adharma, and the eventual defeat of Ravan connects directly to the meaning of Vijayadashami. The film's grand battles, mythological characters, powerful weapons, and larger-than-life settings make it suitable for a Dasara-themed watchlist.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ashish Shelar meets Tiger Shroff after Juhu firing incident, Checks on actor’s well-being
articles.summary: Maharashtra Minister Ashish Shelar met with Bollywood star Tiger Shroff following the firing incident in Mumbai.
articles.body: Maharashtra Minister Ashish Shelar met with Bollywood star Tiger Shroff following the firing incident in Mumbai. Ashish Shelar shared a few pictures from his meeting with Tiger. Tiger could be seen sporting a black vest as he was engaged in a conversation with Shelar and others."Visited Tiger Shroff and enquired about his well-being following the unfortunate firing incident in Juhu. Such acts of violence have no place in our society. Wishing him strength and a speedy recovery," Shelar posted.Meanwhile, the Mumbai Police has taken custody of three suspects arrested in Rajasthan’s Kota in connection with the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff's car.A local court granted the police a 48-hour transit remand, allowing the Maharashtra Police team to take custody of the accused and transport them to Mumbai for further investigation.The suspects are expected to undergo detailed interrogation in Mumbai as investigators probe the circumstances surrounding the firing incident and their alleged involvement in the case.Speaking on the matter, Kota Additional SP Subhash Chandra Mishra told the media, "After being arrested yesterday, they were produced before the competent court for a transit remand. The court granted the transit remand, following which they were handed over to the Mumbai Police. They stayed here overnight, partly because the police team had been travelling for a long time and were exhausted, and also because they had put significant effort into the interrogation. For security and safety reasons, it was deemed necessary that they not depart during the night; hence, they stayed here... Regarding the Kota Police's involvement: we will provide security as requested by the Mumbai Police team... if they request security for a specific duration or distance, we will provide it; otherwise, our responsibility extends up to the state border...."Earlier, Mumbai Police executed an alternative strategy, dubbed 'Plan B', to secure the three shooters. They were kept at the Railway Colony police station throughout the night. Visuals from the Kota Railway Colony police station showed tight security arrangements, with teams from the Mumbai Police Crime Branch and Rajasthan Police maintaining a security cordon around the premises.According to reports, the Mumbai Police received instructions to follow ‘Plan B’ for transporting the accused. As a result, the police reportedly changed their original plan to take the accused to Mumbai overnight and decided to keep them in Kota.Speaking on the same, Ramswaroop Meena, SHO at Railway Colony Police Station, explained that the three accused have been granted a 48-hour transit remand and are being transported to Mumbai by the Maharashtra Police.The case pertains to the firing that took place around 7 pm on Sunday in the Juhu area of Mumbai, when actor Tiger Shroff was leaving a football club. The accused allegedly opened fire at the actor’s car. Although the actor escaped direct gunshot injuries, his driver sustained injuries in the incident.According to the police, the accused were caught while travelling on a train. A case has been registered under Sections 109(1) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 3 and 25 of the Arms Act. articles.title: Christian Horner: Kimi Antonelli has 'earned' the right to be Mercedes' number one
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli is on course to become F1's youngest world champion and earn the right for Mercedes to pick him as its number-one driver over George Russell
articles.body:
Christian Horner reckons the soon-to-be Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli has 'earned' his right to become the outright number-one driver at Mercedes after a dominant 2026.

The 20-year-old holds a 102-point lead over team-mate George Russell in second with six rounds remaining this season, so he can clinch the title in Austin next time out.

Antonelli has achieved this in only his second year of F1 and thanks to 14 podiums including eight wins, while he has had the upper hand on Russell who entered 2026 as the title favourite.

So Horner thinks Antonelli is the man to lead the dominant Mercedes forwards if another squad becomes a threat, amid an ongoing debate over whether teams should prioritise a driver.

Horner's Red Bull outfit was often in favour of this during his time as team boss from 2005 to 2025, first with Sebastian Vettel and then Max Verstappen - both of whom won four world titles each.

McLaren , for example, had a contrasting approach last year with Oscar Piastri and eventual champion Lando Norris , who were given equal treatment but almost beaten by Verstappen.

Or, as referred to by Horner, in 1986 when Williams produced the constructors' title-winning FW11 for Nigel Mansell and Nelson Piquet, who lost the drivers' crown to McLaren's Alain Prost.

Mansell's hopes of winning the 1986 title dramatically ended with an exploding tyre at the Australia finale

"It's very hard to keep everybody happy all the time," Horner told Autosport. "You've just got to be honest and with the principles of 'okay, what are the objectives here'.

"At the end of the day, the team is what comes first and the drivers are ultimately contractors. To promise both drivers that you can be able to win a world championship is unrealistic.

"Ultimately there will be one driver that achieves superiority on track and they're both given the same chance, they're both given the same equipment, but you earn the respect and a status within a team by what you do on a track.

"It's like Kimi Antonelli at the moment. He's earning that position in that team by what he's doing on circuit and if there came to a tight fight between him and a rival from another team, the team would have to take a stance.

"Otherwise they risk losing a championship in the way that Williams potentially did with Mansell and Piquet against Prost all those years ago. So it's just how you set your stall out to go racing."

The motivation behind Red Bull always picking a number one perhaps stemmed from 2010 when Vettel and team-mate Mark Webber often collided while vying for the title.

It almost led to Ferrari 's Fernando Alonso clinching that championship, but then from 2011 Vettel asserted dominance over Webber with Verstappen doing similar over his various team-mates.

Everything at Red Bull is built around Verstappen

"What it taught me in the early days, we were a young team, we just started winning and then all the pressures that go with winning and the expectations suddenly rise," added Horner.

"The media scrutiny and the spotlight is on you, everything is being analysed to the nth degree and you've just got to stick to your principles.

"You can't keep everybody happy all of the time and it's doing what is best for the team.

"That's what my job was, I was employed to do the best for Red Bull Racing which meant winning."

articles.body: Vidyut Jammwal has predicted a promising future for Sivakarthikeyan in the action genre, saying the Tamil actor has the potential to become one of the biggest action stars of his generation. In a recent interview, Jammwal praised his 'Madharaasi' co-star and revisited his experience of working with Vijay in the 2012 blockbuster 'Thuppakki'. The actor also recalled how the film introduced him to the excitement of a major box-office success, years before his Hollywood debut in Street Fighter.Vidyut Jammwal says Sivakarthikeyan could become one of this generation’s biggest action starsVidyut Jammwal has high praise for Sivakarthikeyan, with whom he shared screen space in A.R. Murugadoss’ Tamil action thriller 'Madharaasi'. Jammwal played the antagonist in the 2025 film, which featured Sivakarthikeyan in the lead. Reflecting on their collaboration in a conversation with The Hollywood Reporter, the action star said he could recognise his co-star’s potential through their work together.“Siva's brilliant... Murugadoss would not find somebody who he doesn't believe is brilliant,” Jammwal said, acknowledging the filmmaker’s confidence in the actor.He went on to make a strong prediction about Sivakarthikeyan’s future in action cinema. “I would say he could be one of this generation’s big action stars very soon. I've worked with him, and being an action-oriented actor myself, every time I perform with somebody, I know their potential,” he said.Jammwal’s assessment carries particular weight given his own experience in action films, including the 'Commando' franchise.Vidyut Jammwal recalls how ‘Thuppakki’ became his first major box-office hitJammwal also looked back at 'Thuppakki', the 2012 Tamil action thriller directed by A.R. Murugadoss and starring Vijay. The film featured Jammwal as the antagonist and proved to be a significant turning point in his career. It was also his first experience of being part of a major commercial success.“My experience with Vijay was a little different because that was my first big hit that I had experienced. I didn't know what a hit was, till 'Thuppakki' had released and blew up,” he recalled.The film’s reception was so encouraging that Jammwal remembers travelling to Chennai to celebrate its success on the day it released.“The movie had released and it was Friday evening. I was on my flight to Chennai to celebrate the success, because we already knew it was doing do well,” he said.The experience offered Jammwal an early glimpse of the scale of a successful theatrical release. In the years since, he has built a career around physically demanding action roles, while continuing to work across Hindi and South Indian cinema.A.R. Murugadoss connects Vidyut Jammwal’s ‘Thuppakki’ and ‘Madharaasi’ experiencesMurugadoss played a significant role in both milestones Jammwal discussed. The filmmaker directed 'Thuppakki', which starred Vijay, and later cast Jammwal opposite Sivakarthikeyan in 'Madharaasi'. In both films, Jammwal took on the antagonist’s role, giving him the opportunity to work with two prominent Tamil stars at different stages of their careers.Vidyut Jammwal makes his Hollywood debut with ‘Street Fighter’Jammwal’s career is now entering a new phase with 'Street Fighter', directed by Kitao Sakurai. Based on the popular video game franchise, the film marks his Hollywood debut, with the actor playing Dhalsim, the Indian yogi and martial artist.The film was released internationally in October 2026.
